newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Gold revaluation cannot aid EU budgets-Maystadt.
newsitem.headline: Gold revaluation cannot aid EU budgets-Maystadt.

text.p: Belgian Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt on Thursday said he did not believe that a revaluation of gold reserves by European central banks could lower government budget deficits or debt.
Speaking to reporters after a meeting with a committee of the European Parliament, Maystadt said: "I don't see how it's possible to translate the revaluation to a reduction in public deficits."

Maystadt cautioned, however, that a favourable decision by Eurostat, the EU's statisical office, on the proposed plan by German Finance Minister Theo Waigel was a possibility, and if approved would have to apply to all EU countries. "If (Germany) can find a way, it should be possible for other countries," he said.
To bridge a large revenue gap for 1997, Germany has proposed that the Bundesbank revalue its gold reserves to market rates.

Separately, when asked whether he favoured an early announcement of how the EU would fix national currencies against the euro, Maystadt said he agreed with the view of Alexandre Lamfalussy, president of the European Monetary Institute, that such a strategy was desirable.
He added that the announcement of a method to lock exchange rates should be made early next year at the time of the decision on which countries qualify for the single currency.
Maystadt said several options for fixing the conversion rates were under consideration, including an average of historical rates.
But he declined to offer a view on which was the best approach. "I don't have a preference for how it is done," he said.

Asked specifically about Luxembourg's proposal that EU governments should announce the existing central parity rates of the Exchange Rate Mechanism later this year, Maystadt said: "There is a risk it could prejudice the judgment of EMU members." -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
